availableCommands.name: huggingface-skills:hf-cloud-aws-context-discovery
availableCommands.description: (huggingface-skills) Discover the user's local AWS context (active profile, region, account ID, caller identity) at the start of any AWS task. Use this skill before any other AWS work — deploying to SageMaker, creating resources, calling AWS APIs, or anything that touches an AWS account. Use it especially when the user has not specified a region or profile explicitly, when they say things like "use my AWS account", "deploy to AWS", "use my profile", or when about to make any AWS CLI or SDK call. Never guess the region or account ID — always use this skill to read it from the local configuration first.

availableCommands.name: huggingface-skills:hf-cloud-python-env-setup
availableCommands.description: (huggingface-skills) Set up an isolated Python environment for SageMaker / AWS work, with the right Python version and current boto3. Use this skill whenever Python code will be executed for a SageMaker deployment, training job, or any AWS automation — including when about to run `pip install`, when about to invoke `boto3`, when creating or activating a virtualenv, or when the user asks to "set up the environment". Never use system Python and never `pip install` into it. Always isolate. This skill prevents the most common failure modes: wrong Python version, dependency conflicts, and stale SDKs.

availableCommands.name: huggingface-skills:hf-cloud-sagemaker-deployment-planner
availableCommands.description: (huggingface-skills) Plan and coordinate the deployment of a model to Amazon SageMaker AI. Use this skill whenever the user wants to deploy, host, serve, or expose a model on SageMaker or AWS — including phrases like "deploy a model", "host this LLM on AWS", "serve this embedding model", "deploy a reranker", "deploy a text-to-image / diffusion model", "host this for async inference", "create an endpoint", "serve my fine-tuned model", or any request that involves making a model available for inference on AWS. Use this even when the user is vague (e.g. "I just want to get this running on AWS, you figure it out"). Works for text-generation LLMs, embedding models, rerankers, classifiers, text-to-image / diffusion models — picks the right serving stack and chooses between real-time and async inference. This is the entry-point skill for SageMaker deployment work — it asks clarifying questions, picks a deployment pathway, and coordinates the other deployment skills.

availableCommands.name: huggingface-skills:hf-cloud-sagemaker-iam-preflight
availableCommands.description: (huggingface-skills) Ensure a usable SageMaker execution role exists before deploying or training. Use this skill whenever about to create a SageMaker endpoint, model, training job, or any resource that requires an execution role. Use it especially when the user has not provided a role ARN explicitly, when scripts are about to call `iam:CreateRole`, or when an AccessDenied error mentions an IAM action. Never blindly call `iam:CreateRole` — always check for existing roles first. This skill prevents the most common SageMaker deployment failure: trying to create IAM resources from an SSO principal that has no IAM write permissions.

availableCommands.name: huggingface-skills:hf-cloud-sagemaker-production-defaults
availableCommands.description: (huggingface-skills) Create a SageMaker endpoint (real-time, real-time scale-to-zero, or async) with autoscaling, CloudWatch alarms, and tagging enabled by default. Use this skill whenever about to create a SageMaker endpoint, write deployment code that calls `create_endpoint`, or finalize a deployment after the image URI and IAM role are known. Provides deploy.py for real-time endpoints, deploy_ic.py for real-time endpoints that scale to zero instances via inference components, and deploy_async.py for async endpoints (also scale-to-zero). prompt.text:
You are the coder for task VOICE-B in the Natally clean-room repository (cwd is the repo root). Read ONLY: this assignment, DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md §8.1, §12.1 and §16, LIBS/reference/VoiceDownloadStatus.natally-ai-studio.tsx (VOICE-A), your owned files and read-only callees.

HARD RULES: edit only src/voice/index.ts. New module-scope names only if in §16 (pending VOICE rows) or private to your file. No placeholders. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for the whole tree. Do not commit or push. A dev server may already run on port 5180 — use `npx vite --port 5190 --strictPort` for your own checks. Report changed paths, checks run with exit status, and anything you could not decide.

YOUR TASK (CHECKLIST.md)
| VOICE-B | `src/voice/index.ts`: §8.1 items 2–4 on the speaking side — a `speakStream` issued while the model still loads waits and then speaks (never silently dropped); chunks are synthesised ahead (next chunk in the worker while the current plays) so playback is gapless; keep karaoke/mouth events and gesture-gating; verify WebGPU→WASM calibration in `src/atelier-original/services/supertonic.worker.ts` is intact (read-only unless broken — report). | `src/voice/index.ts` | ⬜ |

ARCHITECTURE §8.1
### 8.1 Voice target (operator 2026-11-11 — FROZEN)

The voice is the original Supertonic local model (`onnx-community/Supertonic-TTS-ONNX`, ~262 MB, F4) — no hosted voice.
1. **Loading progress is always visible** — restore the original's
   `VoiceDownloadStatus` (reference: `LIBS/reference/VoiceDownloadStatus.natally-ai-studio.tsx`,
   from rebots-online/natally-ai-studio): a thin bar fixed at the bottom of
   every page (landing and app) while the model downloads or prepares, with
   "Downloading Natally's voice for this device…", `x / y MB` and the
   **percentage**; "Preparing Natally's voice…" while the runtime readies;
   errors shown and retryable. Mounted once in `src/main.tsx`.
2. **Preload from first load** — the model starts loading (idle-scheduled,
   Save-Data respected) as soon as any page loads, so it is ready before the
   first click; a click while it still loads speaks as soon as it is ready.
3. **Calibrate to the device's resources** — WebGPU where available, WASM
   otherwise; a failed GPU runtime falls back to WASM for the session.
4. **Pre-render in the background, play in the foreground** — a passage is
   split into chunks; the next chunk is synthesised in the worker while the
   current one plays, so playback is continuous with no gaps between chunks.



ARCHITECTURE §12.1 (context)
### 12.1 Landing target state (operator 2026-11-11 — FROZEN on Robin's order "assign to coders from checklist")

1. **The landing is the atelier — the app's own signed-out page.** Visitors
   land on the page that comes up today when you click Sign In: `AppShell`'s
   signed-out branch (`src/app/AppShell.tsx`), the big Natally in her atelier
   (`AtelierScene`) with the sign-in card. That page, not `landing.html` /
   `src/landing-original/marketing.tsx`, is the landing: astronatally.com `/`
   serves `app.html`. The marketing port is retired from the landing role.
2. **One click, one sign-in (hard rule).** Sign In launches Google's account
   chooser on that same click. No screen, card or button ever asks someone to
   click to sign in after they already clicked Sign In — offering sign-in and
   then presenting another "click here to sign in" taunts them. A blocked
   popup falls back to Google's redirect from that same click, never to a
   second prompt.
3. **All scrolling text is paginated onto cards.** Every piece of landing copy
   is divided into pages, each page its own small card with the dark purple
   background of the card that today carries the second "click here to sign
   in" (that card's look is kept; its second-click role is removed per item
   2). The cards scroll by; no landing copy remains as plain scrolling text.
4. **Entering the natal-chart content swaps the atelier for the focused
   chart** — when the cards talking about the chart scroll into view (or its
   menu item is chosen), the chart takes focus and fills the stage and the
   atelier becomes the inset (the existing swap, `swapInsetView`).
4a. **A tap focuses the chart** — primary inset behaviour (§4): a tap on the
   floating chart brings it to focus, filling the stage, with the atelier as
   the inset; scrolling and menu items drive the same swap.
4b. **Clicking an element on the chart makes Natally explain it** (§4): a
   click/tap on a hovered planet, sign, house or aspect line brings the chart
   forward and she speaks her passage about that element, highlighting it
   (and every element involved) as she goes — the same `explainTarget` →
   reply driver path the signed-in stage uses.
4c. **The swap is smooth and the atelier inset well placed.** Focusing and
   unfocusing glide — no broken or jarring zoom, no jump, no flash of an
   empty stage. When the atelier is the inset it shows Natally whole and
   readable (her face never cropped), in a corner that covers neither the
   chart's wheel nor the cards.
   Both insets — the chart and Natally's card — are movable and resizable
   (drag to move, corner grips to resize, same card behaviour as §4) so it can always be moved out of the way. The focused
   chart is sized to the visible window: the whole wheel fits, nothing cut
   off at the bottom. Behind the wheel is black space with stars and
   constellations floating by — never purple — focused or floating.
   Every inset — the floating chart and Natally's card — sits wholly inside
   the visible window, never cut off at the bottom or any edge.
   Every symbol on the wheel — planet glyphs, sign glyphs, house numbers,
   degree labels — is legible at every inset size, floating or focused: glyph
   sprites keep a minimum on-screen size (≥ 14 CSS px for glyphs, ≥ 11 px for
   degree text) with enough contrast, never shrinking with the canvas into
   illegibility (operator: "the symbols are illegible").
   From first load, the floating chart is placed just as well: a corner on
   the side away from the cards, clear of Natally's face, at a size where
   every glyph reads (§4 face-aware placement, measured with the card column
   counted as occupied).
5. **Leaving the natal-chart content swaps back** — scrolling out of it or
   choosing a menu item outside it returns the big atelier to the stage and
   the chart to the inset.
5a. **Layout: big atelier, cards off to the side.** The atelier fills the
   stage, big, and fits inside the window: Natally and her crystal ball are
   always whole — never cut off by the bottom of the window (the atelier is
   sized to the visible window height, not taller), nor by the card column
   or the inset. The cards look like the sign-in card and sit off to the side —
   never in the middle over Natally — and neither the cards nor the chart
   cover her; the chart inset keeps its face-aware placement (§4). In both
   states — atelier on the stage or the focused chart on the stage — the cards
   stay off to the side and never obscure the main view.
6. **Roles by domain.** astronatally.com is the landing; the webapp lands on
   asknatally.online. Every way into the app from the landing — Sign In,
   create-your-chart, Top Up, open-my-atelier, the `?app=1` entry — routes to
   asknatally.online, and asknatally.online serves the app at `/`.
7. **Sign-in works on both domains.** Firebase authorized domains include
   astronatally.com, asknatally.online and their `www` hosts (added
   2026-11-11; snapshot in `DOCS/DOMAINS/`). Item 2 holds across the domain
   change: Sign In on astronatally.com runs the Google popup on that click
   (redirect fallback when blocked); on success the visitor continues on
   asknatally.online already signed in — the Google ID token travels in the

  uid=1_36 "A natal chart is a map of the sky at the moment you were born — where each planet stood, and against which sign. I cast yours from your birth date, time and place, and it never changes: it is the one sky that was yours."
  uid=1_37 heading "Every part of it, shown" level="2"
  uid=1_38 "Planets, signs, houses, the lines between them — all of it is drawn on your wheel. When I speak of your Mars or your seventh house, I show you where it sits. You never have to take my word for what is there."
  uid=1_39 heading "Kept for you" level="2"
  uid=1_40 "Your chart stays in the atelier, so coming back never means starting over. And when you want something to hold on to, I write up a keepsake natal report — more on that under Prices."
  uid=1_41 heading "I read it aloud" level="2"
  uid=1_42 "Reading a chart alone is slow work. So I speak. As I talk through yours, my words follow the wheel — the part I am describing comes forward, and the rest waits its turn."
  uid=1_43 heading "Watch while you listen" level="2"
  uid=1_44 "This is not a voice bolted onto a picture. When I say “your Moon in the fourth house”, the wheel shows you your Moon in the fourth house. Ask me to go back, and we go back; ask what something means, and I tell you plainly."
  uid=1_45 heading "At your pace" level="2"
  uid=1_46 "Sit and let me read the whole chart, or stop me anywhere. The reading is yours, to take in whatever order suits you."
  uid=1_47 heading "Talk with me" level="2"
  uid=1_48 "A reading here is a conversation. Bring what is on your mind — work, love, timing, a decision you keep circling — and I answer from your chart, showing you the part I am reading from."
  uid=1_49 heading "Straight answers" level="2"
  uid=1_50 "I won’t soften what your chart says, and I won’t dress it up either. If a placement is complicated, I say so and show you why. If your chart doesn’t speak to something, I’ll tell you that too."
  uid=1_51 heading "Come back any time" level="2"
  uid=1_52 "The atelier keeps your chart and our conversation. Come back tomorrow with a new question, and we pick up where we left off."
  uid=1_53 heading "What things cost" level="2"
  uid=1_54 "Casting your natal chart is free — no trial, no lock-in; the chart is yours. Beyond that, you pay for conversation, and only when you choose to."
  uid=1_55 heading "Conversation credits" level="2"
  uid=1_56 "Talking with me runs on credits, bought as packs of US$5, US$10 or US$25. Buy what you need when you need it; nothing renews on its own."
  uid=1_57 heading "Keepsake natal report — US$30" level="2"
  uid=1_58 "For US$30 I write your full natal report: every planet, sign and house in your chart, in my own words. You receive it as a PDF to keep, and as an interactive viewer that stays in the atelier."
  uid=1_59 heading "Learn as we go" level="2"
  uid=1_60 "You don’t need to know astrology to be read to, but you are welcome to learn. Beside our conversation I keep a small notebook — a short note on whatever the sky is teaching us."
  uid=1_61 heading "The notebook grows with you" level="2"
  uid=1_62 "Each lesson stands on its own: what a house is, why the Moon moves fast and Saturn doesn’t, what an aspect does. Read them in order, or just the one you need for the question at hand."
  uid=1_63 heading "No gatekeeping" level="2"
  uid=1_64 "Astrology has enough jargon for three trades. Anything I use, I explain — in the reading, in the notebook, whenever you ask."

  uid=1_30 "Free — sign in with Google."
  uid=1_31 heading "What happens here" level="2"
  uid=1_32 "You give me your birth date, time and place. I cast your natal chart — the sky at the moment you were born — and we look at it together. When I mention your Mars or your seventh house, you can see exactly where it sits."
  uid=1_33 heading "Open from your first visit" level="2"
  uid=1_34 "Casting your chart is free, and the atelier keeps it for your next visit. What anything further costs is written further down this page, plainly."
  uid=1_35 heading "Your chart, cast for you alone" level="2"
  uid=1_36 "A natal chart is a map of the sky at the moment you were born — where each planet stood, and against which sign. I cast yours from your birth date, time and place, and it never changes: it is the one sky that was yours."
  uid=1_37 heading "Every part of it, shown" level="2"
  uid=1_38 "Planets, signs, houses, the lines between them — all of it is drawn on your wheel. When I speak of your Mars or your seventh house, I show you where it sits. You never have to take my word for what is there."
  uid=1_39 heading "Kept for you" level="2"
  uid=1_40 "Your chart stays in the atelier, so coming back never means starting over. And when you want something to hold on to, I write up a keepsake natal report — more on that under Prices."
  uid=1_41 heading "I read it aloud" level="2"
  uid=1_42 "Reading a chart alone is slow work. So I speak. As I talk through yours, my words follow the wheel — the part I am describing comes forward, and the rest waits its turn."
  uid=1_43 heading "Watch while you listen" level="2"
  uid=1_44 "This is not a voice bolted onto a picture. When I say “your Moon in the fourth house”, the wheel shows you your Moon in the fourth house. Ask me to go back, and we go back; ask what something means, and I tell you plainly."
  uid=1_45 heading "At your pace" level="2"
  uid=1_46 "Sit and let me read the whole chart, or stop me anywhere. The reading is yours, to take in whatever order suits you."
  uid=1_47 heading "Talk with me" level="2"
  uid=1_48 "A reading here is a conversation. Bring what is on your mind — work, love, timing, a decision you keep circling — and I answer from your chart, showing you the part I am reading from."
  uid=1_49 heading "Straight answers" level="2"
  uid=1_50 "I won’t soften what your chart says, and I won’t dress it up either. If a placement is complicated, I say so and show you why. If your chart doesn’t speak to something, I’ll tell you that too."
  uid=1_51 heading "Come back any time" level="2"
  uid=1_52 "The atelier keeps your chart and our conversation. Come back tomorrow with a new question, and we pick up where we left off."
  uid=1_53 heading "What things cost" level="2"
  uid=1_54 "Casting your natal chart is free — no trial, no lock-in; the chart is yours. Beyond that, you pay for conversation, and only when you choose to."
  uid=1_55 heading "Conversation credits" level="2"
  uid=1_56 "Talking with me runs on credits, bought as packs of US$5, US$10 or US$25. Buy what you need when you need it; nothing renews on its own."
  uid=1_57 heading "Keepsake natal report — US$30" level="2"
  uid=1_58 "For US$30 I write your full natal report: every planet, sign and house in your chart, in my own words. You receive it as a PDF to keep, and as an interactive viewer that stays in the atelier."
  uid=1_59 heading "Learn as we go" level="2"
  uid=1_60 "You don’t need to know astrology to be read to, but you are welcome to learn. Beside our conversation I keep a small notebook — a short note on whatever the sky is teaching us."
  uid=1_61 heading "The notebook grows with you" level="2"
  uid=1_62 "Each lesson stands on its own: what a house is, why the Moon moves fast and Saturn doesn’t, what an aspect does. Read them in order, or just the one you need for the question at hand."
  uid=1_63 heading "No gatekeeping" level="2"
  uid=1_64 "Astrology has enough jargon for three trades. Anything I use, I explain — in the reading, in the notebook, whenever you ask."

  uid=3_28 "I’m Natally. I keep an atelier for charts. Sit down with me and I’ll cast yours, then talk it over with you — speaking as I go, with your wheel in view the whole time."
  uid=3_29 button "Create your natal chart — it's free"
  uid=3_30 "Free — sign in with Google."
  uid=3_31 heading "What happens here" level="2"
  uid=3_32 "You give me your birth date, time and place. I cast your natal chart — the sky at the moment you were born — and we look at it together. When I mention your Mars or your seventh house, you can see exactly where it sits."
  uid=3_33 heading "Open from your first visit" level="2"
  uid=3_34 "Casting your chart is free, and the atelier keeps it for your next visit. What anything further costs is written further down this page, plainly."
  uid=3_35 heading "Your chart, cast for you alone" level="2"
  uid=3_36 "A natal chart is a map of the sky at the moment you were born — where each planet stood, and against which sign. I cast yours from your birth date, time and place, and it never changes: it is the one sky that was yours."
  uid=3_37 heading "Every part of it, shown" level="2"
  uid=3_38 "Planets, signs, houses, the lines between them — all of it is drawn on your wheel. When I speak of your Mars or your seventh house, I show you where it sits. You never have to take my word for what is there."
  uid=3_39 heading "Kept for you" level="2"
  uid=3_40 "Your chart stays in the atelier, so coming back never means starting over. And when you want something to hold on to, I write up a keepsake natal report — more on that under Prices."
  uid=3_41 heading "I read it aloud" level="2"
  uid=3_42 "Reading a chart alone is slow work. So I speak. As I talk through yours, my words follow the wheel — the part I am describing comes forward, and the rest waits its turn."
  uid=3_43 heading "Watch while you listen" level="2"
  uid=3_44 "This is not a voice bolted onto a picture. When I say “your Moon in the fourth house”, the wheel shows you your Moon in the fourth house. Ask me to go back, and we go back; ask what something means, and I tell you plainly."
  uid=3_45 heading "At your pace" level="2"
  uid=3_46 "Sit and let me read the whole chart, or stop me anywhere. The reading is yours, to take in whatever order suits you."
  uid=3_47 heading "Talk with me" level="2"
  uid=3_48 "A reading here is a conversation. Bring what is on your mind — work, love, timing, a decision you keep circling — and I answer from your chart, showing you the part I am reading from."
  uid=3_49 heading "Straight answers" level="2"
  uid=3_50 "I won’t soften what your chart says, and I won’t dress it up either. If a placement is complicated, I say so and show you why. If your chart doesn’t speak to something, I’ll tell you that too."
  uid=3_51 heading "Come back any time" level="2"
  uid=3_52 "The atelier keeps your chart and our conversation. Come back tomorrow with a new question, and we pick up where we left off."
  uid=3_53 heading "What things cost" level="2"
  uid=3_54 "Casting your natal chart is free — no trial, no lock-in; the chart is yours. Beyond that, you pay for conversation, and only when you choose to."
  uid=3_55 heading "Conversation credits" level="2"
  uid=3_56 "Talking with me runs on credits, bought as packs of US$5, US$10 or US$25. Buy what you need when you need it; nothing renews on its own."
  uid=3_57 heading "Keepsake natal report — US$30" level="2"
  uid=3_58 "For US$30 I write your full natal report: every planet, sign and house in your chart, in my own words. You receive it as a PDF to keep, and as an interactive viewer that stays in the atelier."
  uid=3_59 heading "Learn as we go" level="2"
  uid=3_60 "You don’t need to know astrology to be read to, but you are welcome to learn. Beside our conversation I keep a small notebook — a short note on whatever the sky is teaching us."
  uid=3_61 heading "The notebook grows with you" level="2"
  uid=3_62 "Each lesson stands on its own: what a house is, why the Moon moves fast and Saturn doesn’t, what an aspect does. Read them in order, or just the one you need for the question at hand."
  uid=3_63 heading "No gatekeeping" level="2"
  uid=3_64 "Astrology has enough jargon for three trades. Anything I use, I explain — in the reading, in the notebook, whenever you ask."
